title_zh: 连环画《三国演义31：三气周瑜》
title_en: Comic Book 'Romance of the Three Kingdoms 31: Three Times Outwitting Zhou Yu'
source_file: 连环画《三国演义31：三气周瑜》（7-11岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 三氣周瑜
三氣周瑜
（三国演义之三十一）
王星北 改编
汪玉山 绘画

[P2] 内容提要
上集“甘露寺”，叙孙权用周瑜之计，软
困刘备在东吴，要刘备将荆州交还。后来
刘备娶了孙权的妹妹，逃回荆州。
本集叙周瑜再用计策，明取西川，暗奔荆州。
又被诸葛亮识破，伏兵截击。周瑜败回，气愤而死。
下集“反西凉”，叙马超起兵，入关报仇，大败
曹操于潼关。

1. 周瑜被诸葛亮预先埋伏三支军马，一击大败。众将把他救醒，开
船逃回柴桑。周瑜又气又恨，口口声声要和诸葛亮拼个死活。

[P3] 2. 周瑜自忖计策屡次失败，没有面目去见吴侯。便连夜上书孙权，请他兴兵雪恨。
3. 孙权正在等待消息，忽报蒋钦等四将已经回来，却没有捉住刘备。孙权大怒，拍着案桌传四将进见。

[P4] 4. 四将拜见孙权。蒋钦交还佩剑，禀明经过。孙权气得横眉怒目，大骂刘备。
5. 正在恼怒，忽然周瑜差人送来书信。孙权拆信一看，更加气愤，要拜程普为都督，立即起兵去取荆州。

[P5] 6. 张昭竭力谏阻。他说：‘曹操怕我们与刘备联合，所以不敢来报‘赤壁之仇’。现在我们自相吞并，曹操必然乘虚来攻，那就危险了。’
7. 顾雍想出一条计策：派人到许都去，表奏刘备为荆州牧，使曹操知道孙、刘联合，不敢用兵江南。再用反间计，令曹、刘自相攻击，乘机夺回荆州。

[P6] 8. 孙权听了顾雍的话，气也平了。便派华歆送表到许都去。
9. 华歆到了许都，听说曹操到邺都去了，在那里庆贺铜雀台的落成，便又赶到邺都去候见。

[P7] 10. 军吏报告曹操，说东吴派华歆来表奏刘备为荆州牧。孙权的妹妹嫁给刘备，荆、襄九郡都属刘备所有了。
11. 曹操正在兴头上，准备写诗来庆祝铜雀台，一听这消息，手忙脚乱，笔也掉落地上。

[P8] 12. 程昱问他为何这样吃惊。曹操叹了一口气说：“刘备好像一条龙，被困在陆地上。现在得了荆州，譬如放入大海，就难制伏了。
13. 程昱又说：“孙权派华歆来表奏刘备，是有用意的。孙权本来忌刘备，屡次想夺取荆州；就怕丞相乘虚去攻击他。这样，即使刘备安心，又料丞相不敢去打江南。”

[P9] 东吴所依靠的是周瑜。现在丞相可表
奏周瑜为南郡太守，程普为江夏太守，
把华歆留在朝中重用。这样，周瑜无后
顾之忧，就会一心对付刘备去了。
14. 曹操点点头，说他料得不错。程昱又献个计策，使孙、刘自相吞
并，自己却从中取事，一下子便可击破两个敌人。曹操大喜，就依计
行事。
15. 曹操便召华歆上台，重加赏赐。

[P10] 16. 曹操和百官回到许昌，表奏周瑜为总领南郡太守，程普为江夏太守。封华歆为大理寺卿，留在许都。并派人到东吴去。
17. 使命到了东吴，孙权自然放下心来。周瑜、程普都拜受了南郡太守和江夏太守的职位。

[P11] 18. 周瑜就职以后，更想报仇，便写了封信给孙权，请他派鲁肃去讨还荆州。
19. 孙权看了信，便问鲁肃：‘刘备要等什么时候还荆州？’鲁肃呆了一会说：‘文书上明白写着，得了西川便还。’

[P12] 20. 孙权脸色一沉，怒冲冲地说：“只说去取，至今又不动兵，不等老了人！”鲁肃是保人，便说：“让我到荆州去，催他赶快交还。”
21. 鲁肃到了荆州。孔明料知鲁肃来意，便与刘备商量好应付的办法。刘备接鲁肃进府，鲁肃说：“吴侯派我来问皇叔，现在两家结了亲，当看亲戚情面，请皇叔交还荆州。”

[P13] 22. 谁知刘备沉默了一阵，忽然放声大哭起来。这一来，倒把鲁肃迷糊了。他慌忙站起来说：“皇叔有话好说，为什么这样伤心？”
23. 刘备却不理睬，捂着脸，仍是哭个不停。原来，刘备听说鲁肃前来，事先和孔明商量好，孔明要他这样做的。

[P14] 24. 鲁肃正在疑惑，只见孔明从屏后出来，说：“我刚才已听见了，子敬知道我主公哭的缘故吗？”鲁肃道：“这，我实在猜不出！
25. 孔明说：“这有什么难猜的呢！西川刘璋，是我主的同宗兄弟，起兵去取他的城池，在理不通。要不取，还了荆州，又到哪里去安身？不还，亲戚面上又不好看。事出两难，所以伤心。”

[P15] 请子敬将皇叔烦恼情节，回告吴侯，这事缓几时再说。
皇叔不必烦恼，有事我们好商量。
26. 刘备听了，挑动心事，真的搥胸跺脚，放声大哭。鲁肃没了主意，本来是讨荆州来的，现在却变成安慰刘备来了。孔明又请鲁肃照实去回复吴侯。
27. 鲁肃道：“如果吴侯不从，怎么办呢？”孔明道：“吴侯和皇叔是至亲，怎么会不肯呢？请你婉言回复。”鲁肃见刘备这样哀痛，只得答应了。

[P16] 28. 刘备才止住悲伤，擦一下眼泪，向鲁肃道谢。孔明又竭力恳托。鲁肃便告别回去了。
29. 鲁肃怕孙权责怪，不去南徐，却先到柴桑来和周瑜商量。周瑜一听，急得连连跺着脚说：“你又中了诸葛亮的计策了，这是推托。我看这事还要连累老兄！”

[P17] 30. 鲁肃很是不安。周瑜却叫他再去见刘备，说刘备不去取西川，我东吴去取；东吴取得西川，便作嫁资，但要把荆州交还东吴。鲁肃说：“西川这么远，攻取却非容易。”
31. 周瑜说：“你真是个老实人，我不过以此为名，使刘备不做准备罢了。东吴军马路过荆州时，要刘备供应钱粮。等刘备出城劳军，乘势杀了他，夺取荆州。”鲁肃恍然大悟，便又往荆州去。

[P18] 32. 刘备知道鲁肃又来，疑惑不定。孔明说：“鲁肃必不曾见吴侯，只到柴桑和周瑜商量好什么计策，来诱骗我们。但是他说的话，主公只看我点头，便答应他好了。”
33. 鲁肃见了刘备，说：“吴侯称赞皇叔的品德，想出兵替皇叔收取西川，取了西川便作嫁资，那时换回荆州。”

[P19] 34. 孔明听了，点点头说：“难得吴侯好心！”刘备忙拱手称谢：“全仗子敬大力，我很感激。雄师到日，即当远接犒劳。”
35. 鲁肃暗喜，辞别回去。刘备不明白，问孔明。孔明大笑着说：“周瑜死日到了！这等计策，怎能瞒得过我！他假说取川，实际上是乘我不备，袭取荆州。主公放心，我自有安排。”

[P20] 36. 孔明便唤赵云等将进来，吩咐他们按计行事。
37. 再说鲁肃回见周瑜，说刘备准备出城劳军。周瑜大笑着说：‘诸葛亮今番也中了我计！’便教鲁肃回报吴侯，并派程普引军接应。

[P21] 38. 周瑜这时箭疮已经全愈，便令甘宁为先锋，自己和徐盛、丁奉为中军，凌统、吕蒙为后队。水陆大兵五万，望荆州而来。
39. 周瑜亲自带领水师，他坐在船头上，笑容满面，以为孔明中计。

[P22] 40. 前军到了夏口。周瑜向前了望，远远有只小船破浪驶来。左右回报：刘皇叔派糜竺来见都督。

41. 糜竺上了大船，见过周瑜，说：“钱粮都准备好了。主公在荆州门外迎候都督。”周瑜心中暗喜，却叫糜竺先回去通知刘备。
你回去见皇叔，说这次出兵远征，都是为了你们的事，皇叔劳军须要郑重。

[P23] 42. 糜竺下小船回去后，周瑜把战船排列整齐，依次前进。看看来到公安，并无一只军船，又无一人远接。周瑜催船速行。
43. 快到荆州的时候，只见江面上静悄悄的还是没有一只船。哨探回报：“荆州城上，插两面白旗，并无一人。”周瑜心里疑惑，令军士把船靠岸。

[P24] 44. 他上岸骑马，带了甘宁等一班将官，引亲随精兵三千人，如飞地向荆州城赶去。
45. 到了城下，果见城头上插着两面白旗，却不见一个人影。周瑜连忙勒住马，令军士去叫门。

[P25] 46. 城上问是谁人。吴军答道：“是东吴周都督亲自在此！”
47. 说声未了，忽然一声梆子响，城上一齐竖起刀枪。赵云威风凛凛地站在敌楼上，高声叫道：“都督为何到这里来？”周瑜说：“我替你们去取西川，难道你不知道么？”

[P26] 48. 赵云却指着周瑜大笑着说：‘孔明军师已知都督的计策，所以留我在这里等候。我主公说，东吴如果真的去取西川，他当从此隐避山林，决不失信于天下。’
49. 周瑜一听，也不说话，拨转马头就走。

[P27] 50. 行不到半里，只见一人打着令字旗，飞奔到马前报道：“诸葛亮派关羽、张飞、黄忠、魏延四路兵马，从四面杀来。喊声震天，都说要捉都督。”
51. 周瑜大叫一声，从马上倒栽下来，众将慌忙把他扶起，救回船去。

[P28] 52. 军士纷纷传说：刘备与孔明在前面山顶上喝酒取乐。周瑜越加愤怒，咬牙切齿说：“你道我取不得西川，我偏要去取。”
53. 正在发怒，忽然孙权的弟弟孙瑜来到。周瑜备说前情。孙瑜气愤地说：“诸葛亮欺人太甚，笑我东吴无人！我奉兄长的命令来帮助都督，请都督定夺。”

[P29] 54. 周瑜决定去取西川，令军士赶快开船。来到巴丘，探子报称：
“上流有刘封、关平两人领军截住水路。”
55. 周瑜越加愤怒，正要催军前进，忽然孔明差人送信到了。

[P30] 56. 信上说，周瑜劳师远征，转运千里，难收全功。况且曹操想报赤壁之仇，倘若他乘虚来攻，江南就不能保了。周瑜读完信，满脸通红，哇的一声，口吐鲜血。
57. 周瑜自从南郡被诸葛亮用计击败，一连三次中了诸葛亮的计策，气愤成疾。他自料活不下去，便叫左右取来纸笔，上书吴侯，荐举鲁肃代他的职位。

[P31] 我一心想尽忠报国，不料命在旦夕。希望你们好好的帮助吴侯，为国家出力。
58. 甘宁等一班将官在旁侍候。他忽然抬起头，望了他们好一会，喘着气说话。众将听了，不禁伤心落泪。
59. 说完，又昏了过去。众将慌忙呼救，周瑜渐渐地睁开眼睛，叹了一口长气说：“既生瑜，何生亮！”连叫几声死去。年纪才三十六岁。

[P32] 60. 孙瑜忙派人带上周瑜的遗书，飞报孙权。孙权拆读遗书，不禁放声大哭。
61. 他呜咽着说：“公瑾有这样的才能，不幸死去，叫我去托付谁呢？”便依照周瑜的意见，命鲁肃为都督，总统兵马。

[P33] 只怕吴中
将士要替周
瑜报仇。
周瑜活着，我也不
怕，何况周瑜已死，
那更不必担心了。
62. 刘备得到周瑜死讯，忙与孔明计议。孔明主张借吊丧为名，亲自
到江东去探探虚实。刘备却不放心。
63. 于是孔明与赵云带着五百军士，备了祭礼，乘船到巴丘去吊丧。

[P34] 64. 半路上，探得鲁肃做了都督，周瑜灵柩已回柴桑。孔明便到柴桑来，鲁肃得报，前来迎接。
65. 周瑜部将见孔明来到，都想杀孔明，只因赵云带剑跟随，不敢下手。

[P35] 66. 孔明叫人摆好祭物，跪下来宣读祭文。他称赞周瑜的才能，又诉说自己的悲伤，辞句悲切，听得鲁肃连连擦泪，众将也很感伤。
67. 孔明读了祭文，便伏地大哭。鲁肃却这样想：“孔明很重情义，倒是公瑾量窄，容不得孔明。”

[P36] 68. 祭毕，鲁肃设宴招待孔明，却不提荆州的事。
69. 孔明辞别鲁肃回船。到了江边，忽然有个穿道袍、戴竹冠的人，一手揪住孔明，大笑着说：‘你一连三次用计，气死了周瑜，却又来吊丧，明欺东吴无人！’

[P37] 70. 孔明一怔，回头一看，却是凤雏先生庞统。孔明也笑了起来，连忙拉住他的手，同到船上去。
71. 两人坐在船中，各诉心事。原来庞统住在江东，过着闲散的生活。孔明料想孙权不会重用他，劝他到荆州来帮助刘备。庞统满口答应。

[P38] 72. 临别，孔明又写了一封荐书给他，自回荆州去了。后来孙权果然不用庞统，庞统来投刘备，做了副军师，帮助他收取西川。（待续）
full_text_en:
[P1] Three Times to Anger Zhou Yu
Three Times to Anger Zhou Yu
(Chapter Thirty-One of Romance of the Three Kingdoms)
Adapted by Wang Xingbei
Illustrated by Wang Yushan

[P2] Content Summary
The previous episode, "Ganlu Temple," tells how Sun Quan used Zhou Yu's strategy to detain Liu Bei in Eastern Wu and demand that Liu Bei return Jingzhou. Later, Liu Bei married Sun Quan's sister and escaped back to Jingzhou.
This episode narrates how Zhou Yu used another strategy, ostensibly to take Xichuan but secretly to attack Jingzhou. However, Zhuge Liang uncovered the plot, ambushed him, and Zhou Yu was defeated and died of anger.
The next episode, "Rebellion in Xiliang," tells of Ma Chao raising troops, entering the pass to avenge, and defeating Cao Cao at Tongguan.

1. Zhou Yu was ambushed by three armies预先 laid by Zhuge Liang and suffered a crushing defeat. His generals rescued him, and he fled back to Chaisang by boat. Zhou Yu was furious and resentful, vowing to fight Zhuge Liang to the death.

[P3] 2. Zhou Yu, realizing his strategies had repeatedly failed, felt he had no face to meet the King of Wu. He immediately wrote a letter to Sun Quan, asking him to raise troops to avenge the humiliation.
3. Sun Quan was waiting for news when suddenly he was informed that Jiang Qin and the other three generals had returned, but had failed to capture Liu Bei. Sun Quan became furious and slammed his desk, summoning the four generals to appear before him.

[P4] 4. The four generals pay homage to Sun Quan. Jiang Qin returns his sword and reports the events. Sun Quan, furious, glares with anger and curses Liu Bei.
5. While still angry, suddenly a messenger from Zhou Yu delivers a letter. Sun Quan opens the letter and becomes even more furious, deciding to appoint Cheng Pu as the commander and immediately raise troops to capture Jingzhou.

[P5] 6. Zhang Zhao strongly advised against it. He said: 'Cao Cao fears that we will ally with Liu Bei, so he dares not come to avenge the 'Battle of Red Cliffs'. Now, if we turn on each other, Cao Cao will surely take advantage and attack us, and that would be dangerous.'
7. Gu Yong devised a strategy: send someone to Xu Du to petition for Liu Bei to be appointed Governor of Jingzhou, so that Cao Cao would know that Sun and Liu are allied and would dare not launch an attack on the southern regions. Then, use a counter-intelligence plot to make Cao and Liu attack each other, and seize Jingzhou at the right moment.

[P6] 8. Sun Quan, after hearing Gu Yong's words, calmed down. He then sent Hua Xin to deliver a memorial to Xu Du.
9. Hua Xin arrived in Xu Du, heard that Cao Cao had gone to Ye Du to celebrate the completion of the Bronze Sparrow Terrace, and hurried to Ye Du to pay his respects.

[P7] 10. A military officer reports to Cao Cao that Eastern Wu has sent Hua Xin to present a memorial to appoint Liu Bei as the Governor of Jingzhou. Sun Quan's sister has married Liu Bei, and the nine commanderies of Jing and Xiang now all belong to Liu Bei.
11. Cao Cao, who was in high spirits and preparing to write a poem to celebrate the completion of the Bronze Sparrow Terrace, became flustered upon hearing this news, dropping his brush to the ground.

[P8] 12. Cheng Yu asked him why he was so shocked. Cao Cao sighed and said, "Liu Bei is like a dragon trapped on land. Now that he has obtained Jingzhou, it's as if he has been released into the sea, making him hard to subdue.
13. Cheng Yu continued, "Sun Quan sent Hua Xun to present a memorial to Liu Bei, and there is a purpose behind it. Sun Quan has always been wary of Liu Bei and has repeatedly wanted to seize Jingzhou; he fears that the Chancellor might take advantage of the situation to attack him. Thus, even if Liu Bei feels secure, he still expects the Chancellor to dare not attack the southern regions."

[P9] The Eastern Wu relies on Zhou Yu. Now, Your Excellency may submit a memorial to appoint Zhou Yu as the Governor of Nan Commandery, Cheng Pu as the Governor of Jiangxia, and keep Hua Xin in the court for important use. This way, Zhou Yu will have no worries behind him and will focus entirely on dealing with Liu Bei.
14. Cao Cao nodded, saying he had judged correctly. Cheng Yu then proposed a strategy: let Sun and Liu destroy each other, while Cao Cao benefits from the situation and can defeat both enemies at once. Cao Cao was delighted and decided to follow the plan.
15. Cao Cao then summoned Hua Xin to the platform and bestowed heavy rewards upon him.

[P10] 16. Cao Cao and his officials returned to Xuchang, where he submitted a memorial to appoint Zhou Yu as the overall commander of Nanjun Prefecture and Cheng Pu as the governor of Jiangxia Prefecture. He also appointed Hua Xin as the Minister of Justice, to remain in Xudu, and sent envoys to Eastern Wu.
17. The mission arrived in Eastern Wu, and Sun Quan naturally felt reassured. Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu both accepted their positions as governors of Nanjun and Jiangxia Prefectures.

[P11] 18. After Zhou Yu took office, he wanted revenge even more, so he wrote a letter to Sun Quan, asking him to send Lu Su to demand the return of Jingzhou.
19. Sun Quan read the letter and asked Lu Su, 'When will Liu Bei return Jingzhou?' Lu Su hesitated for a moment and said, 'The document clearly states he will return it after he obtains Xichuan.'

[P12] 20. Sun Quan's face darkened, and he angrily said, "You keep talking about taking it, but haven't moved a single soldier yet. We won't wait until we're old!" Lu Su, who was the guarantor, replied, "Let me go to Jingzhou and urge him to return it quickly." 
21. Lu Su arrived in Jingzhou. Kong Ming, anticipating Lu Su's purpose, had already discussed a strategy with Liu Bei. Liu Bei welcomed Lu Su into his residence. Lu Su said, "The Lord of Wu sent me to ask your Majesty. Now that our two families are married, please consider the kinship and return Jingzhou."

[P13] 22. Unexpectedly, Liu Bei fell silent for a moment, then suddenly burst into loud sobs. This confused Lu Su. He hurriedly stood up and said, "Your Highness, please speak. Why are you so heartbroken?"
23. Liu Bei ignored him, covering his face and continuing to cry. It turned out that Liu Bei had heard Lu Su was coming, and had previously discussed this with Kong Ming, who had instructed him to act this way.

[P14] 24. Lu Su was puzzled when he saw Kong Ming emerge from behind the screen and say, "I've just heard everything. Zi Jing, do you know why my lord is crying?" Lu Su replied, "This... I truly can't guess!
25. Kong Ming said, "What's so hard to guess? Liu Zhang of Western Shu is my lord's kinsman. To raise troops and seize his cities is unreasonable. If we don't take them, and return Jingzhou, where else can we settle? If we don't return it, it's also awkward for our kinship. Caught between two difficulties, he is heartbroken."

[P15] Please, Zi Jing, report to Lord Wu the details of His Majesty's distress. Let's postpone this matter for a while.
His Majesty need not worry. If there's anything, we can discuss it together.
26. Upon hearing this, Liu Bei was deeply moved, truly beating his chest and stamping his feet, breaking into loud sobs. Lu Su was at a loss; he had originally come to demand Jingzhou, but now he found himself comforting Liu Bei. Kong Ming then asked Lu Su to truthfully report back to Lord Wu.
27. Lu Su asked, "What if Lord Wu refuses? What should we do?" Kong Ming replied, "Lord Wu and His Majesty are close kin. How could he possibly refuse? Please respond with tact." Seeing Liu Bei so grief-stricken, Lu Su had no choice but to agree.

[P16] 28. Liu Bei stopped his sorrow, wiped away a tear, and thanked Lu Su. Kong Ming also pleaded earnestly. Lu Su then bid farewell and left.
29. Lu Su, fearing that Sun Quan would blame him, did not go to Nanxu, but instead went to Chaisang to consult with Zhou Yu. Upon hearing this, Zhou Yu became anxious and stamped his feet, saying, “You’ve fallen for Zhuge Liang’s scheme again. This is just an excuse. I fear this matter will still involve you, brother!”

[P17] 30. Lu Su was very uneasy. Zhou Yu told him to go see Liu Bei again, saying that if Liu Bei didn't go to take Western Shu, then Wu would; if Wu took Western Shu, it would be as a dowry, but Liu Bei must return Jingzhou to Wu. Lu Su said, "Western Shu is so far away, it's not easy to attack." 
31. Zhou Yu said, "You are truly a honest man. I only used this as an excuse to make Liu Bei unprepared. When Wu's army passes through Jingzhou, we will ask Liu Bei to supply money and grain. When Liu Bei leaves the city to greet the troops, we will kill him and seize Jingzhou." Lu Su suddenly understood, and then went back to Jingzhou.

[P18] 32. Liu Bei knew Lu Su had come again and was uncertain. Kong Ming said, "Lu Su certainly hasn't seen the Lord of Wu; he only went to Chaisang to discuss some scheme with Zhou Yu, intending to deceive us. But whatever he says, Your Majesty, just look at me and nod, then agree to him." 
33. Lu Su met Liu Bei and said, "The Lord of Wu praises Your Highness's virtue and wishes to send troops to help Your Highness take Western Shu. Once Western Shu is taken, it will serve as a dowry, and then we can exchange it for Jingzhou."

[P19] 34. Kongming listened, nodded, and said, "It's rare to see the Lord of Wu so kind-hearted!" Liu Bei hurriedly bowed and thanked him, "I am deeply grateful for your great effort, Zi Jing. When your mighty army arrives, I will personally welcome and entertain you.
35. Lu Su secretly rejoiced and took his leave. Liu Bei, puzzled, asked Kongming. Kongming laughed loudly, "Zhou Yu's time is up! How could such a scheme deceive me! He pretends to help take Shu, but in reality, he plans to seize Jingzhou while I am unprepared. Your Majesty, rest assured, I have my own plans."

[P20] 36. Kong Ming then summoned Zhao Yun and other generals, instructing them to carry out the plan.
37. Meanwhile, Lu Su returned to see Zhou Yu and reported that Liu Bei was preparing to go out of the city to greet the troops. Zhou Yu laughed and said, 'Zhuge Liang has finally fallen into my trap!' He then ordered Lu Su to report back to the King of Wu and sent Cheng Pu to lead troops to support the operation.

[P21] 38. Zhou Yu, whose arrow wound had now fully healed, ordered Gan Ning as vanguard, himself and Xu Sheng, Ding Feng as the central force, Ling Tong and Lü Meng as the rear guard. With 50,000 troops by land and sea, they marched toward Jingzhou.
39. Zhou Yu personally led the naval forces. Sitting at the bow of the ship, he smiled broadly, believing Kong Ming had fallen into his trap.

[P22] 40. The vanguard reached Xia Kou. Zhou Yu looked ahead and saw a small boat breaking through the waves in the distance. His attendants reported: 'Lord Liu has sent Mi Zhu to see the Commander-in-Chief.'

41. Mi Zhu boarded the large ship, greeted Zhou Yu, and said: 'The money and provisions are all ready. Our Lord is waiting for you outside the gates of Jingzhou.' Zhou Yu was secretly delighted, but told Mi Zhu to return first and inform Liu Bei.
Go back and tell Lord Liu that this campaign is for your sake, and that Lord Liu must personally honor the troops with great solemnity.

[P23] 42. After Mi Zhu returned by small boat, Zhou Yu arranged his warships in order and advanced one by one. Upon arriving at Gong'an, he saw no military ships and no one to greet them from afar. Zhou Yu urged the boats to speed up.
43. As they neared Jingzhou, the river surface was quiet and still empty of any boats. The scout reported: "On the city walls of Jingzhou, two white flags are flying, and there is no one in sight." Zhou Yu felt puzzled and ordered the soldiers to bring the boats to shore.

[P24] 44. He rode ashore, accompanied by General Gan Ning and other officers, leading 3,000 elite troops, galloping swiftly toward the city of Jingzhou.
45. Upon reaching the city gates, he saw two white flags flying atop the city walls, but no one was in sight. Zhou Yu quickly reined in his horse and ordered his soldiers to call out to the gate.

[P25] 46. On the city wall, someone asked who they were. The Wu soldiers replied, "It's the General Zhou of Eastern Wu himself!"
47. Before the words were finished, suddenly a gong sounded, and weapons were raised all over the city wall. Zhao Yun, standing proudly on the enemy tower, shouted loudly, "Why have you, General, come here?" Zhou Yu replied, "I am going to help you take Xichuan. Don't you know that?"

[P26] 48. Zhao Yun pointed at Zhou Yu and laughed, saying, 'Master Kongming has already learned of your strategy, so he left me here to wait. My lord said that if Eastern Wu truly goes to take Xichuan, he will retreat into the mountains and never break his word to the world.'
49. Zhou Yu, upon hearing this, said nothing and turned his horse around to leave.

[P27] 50. After traveling less than half a li, a man carrying a command flag galloped up to the horse and reported: 'Zhuge Liang has sent four armies led by Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Huang Zhong, and Wei Yan, attacking from all directions. The shouts are deafening, and they all say they are here to capture the Commander-in-Chief.'
51. Zhou Yu let out a cry and fell headfirst from his horse. The generals hurriedly lifted him up and carried him back to the ship.

[P28] 52. The soldiers were whispering: Liu Bei and Kong Ming are drinking and having fun on the mountain top ahead. Zhou Yu became even more furious, grinding his teeth and saying, "You think I can't take Xichuan? I'll go and take it anyway!"
53. While still angry, suddenly Sun Quan's younger brother, Sun Yu, arrived. Zhou Yu recounted the previous events. Sun Yu angrily said, "Zhuge Liang is too arrogant, mocking our Eastern Wu as having no capable men! I have come here on my elder brother's orders to assist the Commander. Please, Commander, make your decision."

[P29] 54. Zhou Yu decided to go and capture Xichuan, ordering the soldiers to set sail quickly. Upon arriving at Bachu, a scout reported: 
"Upstream, Liu Feng and Guan Ping are leading troops to block the waterway." 
55. Zhou Yu became even more furious, about to urge his army forward, when suddenly a messenger sent by Kong Ming arrived with a letter.

[P30] 56. The letter said that Zhou Yu's army was exhausted from a long campaign, transporting supplies over thousands of miles, and would find it hard to achieve complete success. Moreover, Cao Cao wanted to avenge the defeat at Red Cliffs; if he attacked while Zhou Yu was away, the southern lands could not be protected. After reading the letter, Zhou Yu turned red in the face, let out a cry, and spat blood.
57. Since being defeated by Zhuge Liang's stratagem at Nanjun, Zhou Yu had fallen victim to Zhuge Liang's schemes three times in a row, becoming so angry that he fell ill. Realizing he would not survive, he ordered his attendants to bring paper and brush, and wrote to the King of Wu, recommending Lu Su to take his position.

[P31] I have always wanted to serve my country with loyalty, but I did not expect to be facing death so soon. I hope you will help the Lord of Wu and serve the nation well.
58. Gan Ning and other generals stood by. He suddenly raised his head, looked at them for a while, and spoke with labored breath. The generals, upon hearing this, could not help but shed tears.
59. After speaking, he fainted again. The generals hurriedly called for help. Zhou Yu slowly opened his eyes, sighed deeply, and said, "Since I was born, why was Zhuge Liang born?" He called out several times before dying, only thirty-six years old.

[P32] 60. Sun Yu hurriedly sent someone with Zhou Yu's will to report to Sun Quan. Sun Quan read the will and couldn't help but burst into tears.
61. He wept, saying, "Gongjin has such talent, yet he died tragically. Who can I entrust my cause to now?" He then followed Zhou Yu's suggestion and appointed Lu Su as the new Commander-in-Chief, to lead all the troops.

[P33] I'm afraid the Wu soldiers might avenge Zhou Yu.
Even if Zhou Yu were alive, I wouldn't fear. How much less should I worry now that he is dead?
62. Liu Bei received news of Zhou Yu's death and hurriedly discussed it with Kong Ming. Kong Ming suggested going to Jiangdong under the pretense of paying respects to investigate the situation. Liu Bei, however, was not at ease.
63. So Kong Ming and Zhao Yun, accompanied by five hundred soldiers and bearing offerings, set sail for Baqiu to pay their respects.

[P34] 64. On the way, they learned that Lu Su had become the commander-in-chief and Zhou Yu's coffin had returned to Chaisang. Kong Ming then went to Chaisang, and Lu Su, upon receiving the news, came to greet him.
65. Zhou Yu's subordinates, upon seeing Kong Ming arrive, all wanted to kill him, but dared not act because Zhao Yun was accompanying him with a sword.

[P35] 66. Kong Ming had the offerings arranged and knelt to read the memorial. He praised Zhou Yu's talent and expressed his own sorrow, his words so heartfelt that Lu Su wiped tears repeatedly, and the other generals were deeply moved.
67. After reading the memorial, Kong Ming fell to the ground and wept bitterly. Lu Su thought to himself, 'Kong Ming is truly a man of deep loyalty and righteousness; it is Gongjin who was narrow-minded and could not tolerate Kong Ming.'

[P36] 68. After the ceremony, Lu Su hosted a banquet for Kong Ming, but did not mention the matter of Jingzhou.
69. Kong Ming bid farewell to Lu Su and returned to his boat. At the riverside, suddenly a man wearing a Daoist robe and a bamboo hat grabbed Kong Ming by the arm and laughed loudly: 'You used your schemes three times in a row, killed Zhou Yu with anger, and yet came to pay your respects—clearly mocking Eastern Wu for having no one!'

[P37] 70. Kong Ming was startled, turned around, and saw it was Mr. Fengchu, Pang Tong. Kong Ming smiled and hurriedly took his hand, bringing him onto the boat.
71. The two sat in the boat, sharing their thoughts. Originally, Pang Tong lived in Jiangdong, leading a leisurely life. Kong Ming thought Sun Quan would not employ him, and advised him to go to Jingzhou to assist Liu Bei. Pang Tong readily agreed.

[P38] 72. Before parting, Kong Ming wrote a letter of recommendation for him and returned to Jingzhou. Later, Sun Quan indeed did not employ Pang Tong, so Pang Tong went to serve Liu Bei, became his deputy military advisor, and helped him conquer Xichuan. (To be continued)
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《三气周瑜》的封面及标题页，标明其为《三国演义》系列之三十一，由王星北改编、汪玉山绘画，画面描绘了两位古装人物在室内对峙的场景。
[P2] 本页为绘本《三气周瑜》的第2页，包含内容提要和第一幅插图。提要回顾了上集情节，介绍了本集周瑜被诸葛亮识破计谋、兵败气愤而死的主线，并预告了下集内容。插图及文字描述了周瑜战败后被救回柴桑，气恨交加，誓与诸葛亮决一死战的场景。
[P3] 本页描绘了周瑜因计策屡次失败而羞愧，连夜上书孙权请求兴兵雪恨；同时，孙权得知蒋钦等四将未能捉住刘备后大怒，传唤四将进见。
[P4] 本页描绘了四将向孙权汇报战败经过，孙权大怒；随后周瑜派人送来书信，孙权读后更加愤怒，决定拜程普为都督，立即起兵攻打荆州。
[P5] 本页描绘了东吴内部对是否攻打荆州的讨论。张昭劝阻孙权，认为与刘备联合可防曹操，自相残杀则危险；顾雍则提出借表奏刘备为荆州牧，使曹操误判孙刘联盟，再用反间计让曹刘相攻，从而夺回荆州的计策。
[P6] 孙权采纳顾雍建议后派华歆送表至许都，华歆得知曹操在邺都庆贺铜雀台落成，便赶往邺都拜见。
[P7] 本页描绘了东吴派华歆向曹操表奏刘备为荆州牧，曹操得知孙权妹妹已嫁刘备、荆襄九郡归刘备所有后，正准备庆祝铜雀台落成时大受打击，惊慌失措。
[P8] 曹操在得知刘备获得荆州后深感忧虑，程昱分析孙权表奏刘备的用意，指出孙权虽忌惮刘备，但更怕曹操趁机进攻，因此此举意在牵制曹操。
[P9] 曹操采纳程昱的计策，决定利用孙刘矛盾，让其自相残杀，自己从中渔利。随后，曹操召见华歆并重加赏赐，以表彰其完成表奏任务。
[P10] 曹操回到许昌后，任命周瑜、程普为荆州地区太守，并派使者前往东吴。东吴收到消息后，孙权放心，周瑜和程普也正式接受任命。
[P11] 周瑜就任后写信给孙权，请求派鲁肃讨还荆州；孙权询问鲁肃，鲁肃回答刘备承诺取得西川后便归还荆州。
[P12] 孙权因刘备未归还荆州而愤怒，派鲁肃前往催讨；鲁肃抵达荆州后，向刘备提出以两家结亲为由，请求归还荆州。
[P13] 鲁肃前来催讨荆州，刘备突然放声大哭，令鲁肃困惑。刘备不理睬鲁肃，继续哭泣，原来这是他与诸葛亮事先商量好的计策。
[P14] 鲁肃对刘备哭泣的原因感到困惑，诸葛亮从屏风后出现，解释刘备因取西川与归还荆州的两难处境而伤心。
[P15] 刘备在诸葛亮的安排下假装悲痛，令鲁肃无法催讨荆州。鲁肃询问对策，诸葛亮以孙刘为至亲为由劝其婉言回复，鲁肃最终答应。
[P16] 刘备在诸葛亮的安排下假装悲痛，成功让鲁肃无法催讨荆州；鲁肃返回后向周瑜汇报，周瑜识破计谋并担心此事会连累自己。
[P17] 周瑜让鲁肃再次去见刘备，以取西川为名，实则计划趁刘备出城劳军时夺取荆州；鲁肃听后恍然大悟，随即前往荆州执行计划。
[P18] 刘备得知鲁肃再次到来，心生疑虑，诸葛亮分析鲁肃此行必有阴谋，并指示刘备只需看其点头即可答应。鲁肃见到刘备后，提出东吴愿出兵助其夺取西川，待成功后以西川作为嫁资，换取荆州。
[P19] 鲁肃假装答应助刘备取西川，实则计划趁机夺取荆州；刘备不知真相，向诸葛亮询问，诸葛亮识破其计谋，表示已自有安排。
[P20] 诸葛亮安排赵云等将领按计行事；鲁肃向周瑜汇报刘备准备出城劳军，周瑜认为计谋得逞，派程普率军接应。
[P21] 周瑜率五万水陆大军进攻荆州，自以为计谋得逞，信心满满。
[P22] 周瑜的军队抵达夏口，刘备派糜竺前来通报。糜竺告知周瑜钱粮已备，刘备将在荆州门外迎候，周瑜暗喜并让糜竺先回去通知刘备，同时嘱咐糜竺转告刘备劳军须郑重。
[P23] 周瑜率军抵达公安后未见迎接，继续前进至荆州时发现江面空无一船，城上插有白旗且无人，心生疑惑并下令靠岸。
[P24] 周瑜率军上岸后，带领甘宁等将领和三千精兵疾驰前往荆州城；抵达城下时，发现城头插有白旗却空无一人，遂勒马令士兵叫门。
[P25] 周瑜率军抵达荆州城下，城上守军询问来者身份，吴军回答是周都督亲至。周瑜正欲进城，城上突然响起梆子声，赵云率军现身，高声质问周瑜来意，周瑜则称自己是来助刘备取西川。
[P26] 赵云识破周瑜计谋，表明刘备已知其意图并坚守信义；周瑜听后无言，立即率军撤退。
[P27] 周瑜率军行进途中，突然接到报告称诸葛亮派关羽、张飞、黄忠、魏延四路兵马从四面杀来，周瑜惊惧交加，从马上倒栽下来，被众将救回船上。
[P28] 周瑜因听闻刘备与诸葛亮在山顶饮酒取乐而更加愤怒，发誓要夺取西川。此时，孙权的弟弟孙瑜前来，表示奉命协助周瑜，并怒斥诸葛亮轻视东吴。
[P29] 周瑜率军前往西川途中，在巴丘得知刘封、关平截断水路，正欲前进时，诸葛亮派人送来书信。
[P30] 周瑜收到诸葛亮的信后，因忧虑战局和曹操趁虚而入而气急攻心，口吐鲜血；随后他因屡次中计、气愤成疾，自知命不久矣，便上书推荐鲁肃接替自己的职位。
[P31] 周瑜病重卧床，临终前嘱咐众将忠于吴国，随后昏厥，醒来后感叹‘既生瑜，何生亮’，最终在三十六岁时去世。
[P32] 周瑜去世后，孙瑜将遗书送至孙权处，孙权悲痛万分，随后依照周瑜遗愿任命鲁肃为都督，统领兵马。
[P33] 刘备得知周瑜去世，与诸葛亮商议后，诸葛亮提议以吊丧为名前往江东探查虚实，但刘备心存疑虑。随后，诸葛亮与赵云率军士备祭礼乘船前往巴丘吊丧。
[P34] 诸葛亮与赵云前往柴桑吊丧，途中得知周瑜灵柩已回，鲁肃接任都督。周瑜旧部欲杀诸葛亮，因赵云带剑护卫而不敢动手。
[P35] 诸葛亮在周瑜灵前设祭，宣读祭文并痛哭，其情真意切令鲁肃和众将动容；鲁肃内心感慨诸葛亮重情义，而周瑜心胸狭隘。
[P36] 诸葛亮祭拜周瑜后，鲁肃设宴款待他但未提荆州之事；诸葛亮辞别回船时，被一名穿道袍戴竹冠的人拦住，指责他用计气死周瑜、借吊丧之名羞辱东吴。
[P37] 诸葛亮在船上遇见庞统，二人相认后同船而行，并在船中交谈。诸葛亮劝说庞统离开江东，前往荆州辅佐刘备，庞统欣然答应。
[P38] 诸葛亮与庞统告别，写信推荐他，自己返回荆州；庞统随后投奔刘备，成为副军师，助其夺取西川。
